name: Auroville
desc: The world's largest and most international intentional township — a universal city dedicated to human unity, inaugurated in 1968 with soil from 124 nations placed in a central urn. Home to ~3,300 residents from 60+ countries across ~20 km².

name: Sadhana Forest
desc: A vegan reforestation community regenerating the endangered Tropical Dry Evergreen Forest on eroded land at Auroville's edge, while raising the local water table. Has hosted 20,000+ international volunteers.

name: Govardhan Ecovillage
desc: An ISKCON-affiliated model farm and spiritual-ecology retreat in the Sahyadri foothills near Mumbai — the first Indian NGO to win a UN World Tourism Organization award.

name: Navdanya / Bija Vidyapeeth
desc: A seed-sovereignty and organic-farming movement founded by Vandana Shiva, whose biodiversity farm and 'Earth University' conserve thousands of indigenous seed varieties.

name: Fireflies Intercultural Centre
desc: An eco-spiritual ashram and retreat south of Bengaluru blending interfaith dialogue, ecological action and personal growth across diverse traditions.

name: SECMOL Campus
desc: A solar-powered alternative school and self-sufficient residential community near Leh, built from earthen techniques and entirely solar-heated even at −25 °C.

name: Ananda Sangha India
desc: The Indian arm of the worldwide Ananda movement of cooperative 'World Brotherhood Colonies' dedicated to Kriya Yoga and meditation, founded by a direct disciple of Yogananda.

name: Sarvodaya Shramadana
desc: Sri Lanka's largest grassroots community-development movement, built on Gandhian-Buddhist principles and active in 15,000+ villages through self-help work-camps.

name: HASERA Permaculture Centre
desc: One of Nepal's leading permaculture research and training centres, grown from a small organic farm in a mountain village; a GEN member.

name: Konohana Family
desc: At the foot of Mount Fuji, ~100 non-blood-related members live and share resources as one extended family, farming 250+ chemical-free crop varieties.

name: Yamagishi (Toyosato)
desc: A network of moneyless, leaderless egalitarian communes; its largest, Toyosato, houses 500+ members practising large-scale organic farming without private money.

name: Pun Pun Center
desc: An organic farm, seed-saving centre and self-reliance community near Chiang Mai, an international hub for natural earth-building.

name: Wongsanit Ashram
desc: A socially-engaged Buddhist spiritual-activist ecovillage and training centre north of Bangkok, grounded in dharma, sustainability and grassroots change.

name: Gaia Ashram
desc: A permaculture ecovillage and learning centre in NE Thailand focused on Ecovillage Design Education, deep ecology and natural building.

name: Brahma Kumaris (Madhuban)
desc: The world's largest woman-led spiritual movement, headquartered at Madhuban — ~1 million students across 8,000+ Raja Yoga centres in 115+ countries, with ~500 permanent residents on campus.

name: Findhorn Ecovillage
desc: One of the world's most influential ecovillages and a global centre for holistic, sustainable living. The 1995 conference here launched the Global Ecovillage Network.

name: Camphill Aberdeen
desc: The original Camphill community, founded by refugees to share life with children and adults with special needs — launching a worldwide movement of 100+ communities.

name: Lammas Ecovillage (Tir y Gafel)
desc: A pioneering off-grid, low-impact ecovillage of nine smallholdings whose landmark planning victory shaped Wales's globally unique 'One Planet Development' policy.

name: Tinker's Bubble
desc: A small low-impact woodland community that bans fossil fuels on site and lives almost entirely from hand- and horse-powered work — a key UK planning precedent.

name: BedZED
desc: The UK's first large-scale carbon-neutral eco-housing development — 82 homes in south London that became an internationally studied model for low-carbon living.

name: LILAC Cohousing
desc: The UK's first affordable straw-bale cohousing scheme, pairing low-impact building with a Mutual Home Ownership Society that ties housing cost to income.

name: Cloughjordan Ecovillage
desc: Ireland's flagship ecovillage, integrated within an existing village, noted for one of the lowest ecological footprints in Ireland.

name: Suderbyn Ecovillage
desc: An experimental international permaculture ecovillage on Baltic Gotland — a living lab for ecotechnology, energy sovereignty and sustainable living.

name: Hurdal Ecovillage
desc: Norway's flagship ecovillage, built around a medieval parish farm; its growth inspired the surrounding municipality to brand itself 'the Sustainable Valley'.

name: Friland
desc: A Danish ecovillage founded around the radical idea of debt-free, self-built homes; residents build by hand from natural and recycled materials.

name: Dyssekilde Ecovillage
desc: One of Denmark's oldest ecovillages, successfully integrated with the village of Torup and known for experimental ecological homes and a community windmill.

name: Freetown Christiania
desc: A self-proclaimed autonomous neighbourhood founded when squatters occupied disused military barracks in central Copenhagen — one of the world's most famous experiments in collective self-governance.

name: Keuruu Ecovillage
desc: An international intentional community on a 54-ha lakeside site in the heart of Finland, combining organic cultivation, natural building and intergenerational life.

name: Sólheimar Ecovillage
desc: Iceland's oldest intentional community and one of the world's first to integrate disabled and non-disabled people, set in a geothermal valley and a Nordic pioneer of organic farming.

name: Sieben Linden
desc: One of Europe's most studied ecovillages, internationally renowned for an extremely low ecological footprint — roughly a quarter to a third of the German average.

name: ZEGG
desc: An ecovillage and international seminar centre SW of Berlin, internationally known for the 'ZEGG Forum' communication method and its open work on community, love and trust.

name: Schloss Tempelhof
desc: A fast-growing ecovillage around a former castle and farm, combining solidarity agriculture, sociocratic governance and alternative education.

name: Lebensgarten Steyerberg
desc: One of Germany's oldest ecovillages, in the restored housing of a former armaments settlement, and a pioneer of permaculture, complementary currencies and Nonviolent Communication.

name: Kommune Niederkaufungen
desc: One of Germany's largest income-sharing communes, founded on egalitarian principles with full communal ownership and consensus decision-making.

name: Krishna Valley
desc: An ISKCON (Hare Krishna) ecovillage and large organic farm — one of the oldest and largest ecovillages in Europe, drawing 25,000–30,000 visitors a year.

name: Schweibenalp
desc: A living-and-working community and seminar centre on an alpine plateau above Lake Brienz (~1,100 m), dedicated to holistic lifestyle and universal spirituality.

name: Schloss Glarisegg
desc: An intentional community and 'place for encounter and consciousness' in a heritage castle estate on Lake Constance, with forest, waterfalls and its own beach.

name: Cambium
desc: An intergenerational ecovillage in Eastern Styria created by converting a former military barracks into housing, co-working, studios and a seminar centre.

name: Wohnprojekt Wien
desc: Austria's largest urban cohousing project — a self-organised community of ~67 adults and 25 children in a 39-unit building on Vienna's former rail lands, a pioneer of sociocracy.

name: EVA-Lanxmeer
desc: A pioneering ecological neighbourhood built around a drinking-water protection zone — often called the largest permaculture settlement in Europe, with ~1,000 inhabitants.

name: Aardehuizen Olst
desc: The first all-Earthship neighbourhood in the Netherlands — 23 self-built earth-and-tyre and straw-bale homes built largely by the residents from recycled materials.

name: Ecodorp Boekel
desc: A climate-positive ecovillage and 'Living Lab' of 36 rental homes designed to showcase regenerative living, with its own energy, food and ecological water purification.

name: Tamera
desc: An internationally renowned 'Healing Biotope' and peace-research centre in SW Portugal — a living laboratory for nonviolent cooperation among humans, nature and animals.

name: Federation of Damanhur
desc: A spiritual ecovillage and federation of self-sustaining communities in northern Italy — famous for the vast underground Temples of Humankind, with its own constitution and currency.

name: Torri Superiore
desc: A restored 14th-century medieval stone village reborn as an ecovillage and cultural association, co-founder of the Italian Ecovillage Network (RIVE).

name: Lakabe
desc: One of Spain's pioneering ecovillages — a medieval village abandoned in the 1960s and reoccupied in 1980, now a fully self-organized community sharing work, money and decisions.

name: Matavenero
desc: A remote car-free 'rainbow' ecovillage in the mountains of León, settled in 1989 in a centuries-old abandoned village, reachable only on foot and living without a formal leader.

name: Valle de Sensaciones
desc: An experimental 'ecovillage laboratory' in the Alpujarra of Granada blending art, sensory experience and ecological living, with treehouses, cave spaces and clay temples.

name: Los Portales
city: El Real de la Jara, Seville
desc: An ecovillage and spiritual community in the Sierra Morena combining organic agriculture, holistic education and a sharing economy with a daily practice of collective dreamwork.

name: Longo maï
desc: A self-managed agricultural and craft cooperative — flagship of a network of ~11 cooperatives across Europe — where ~100 people live, work and run activist campaigns with no salaries.

name: Can Decreix
desc: A small intentional community and research centre on the Franco-Spanish coast that puts the theory of 'degrowth' into daily practice through low-tech living and agroecology.

name: Popolo degli Elfi
desc: The 'People of the Elves' — one of Italy's oldest and most original communities, born from occupying abandoned villages in the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines, living a deliberately low-tech life.

name: Calafou
desc: A 'postcapitalist eco-industrial colony' in a former 19th-century textile colony near Barcelona, combining cooperative housing with collective tech, fabrication and bioarts workshops.

name: Free and Real (Telaithrion)
desc: A Greek non-profit building a prototype self-sufficient eco-community on Mount Telethrion — an open school for sustainability intended to be replicable worldwide.

name: Marinaleda
desc: A self-described 'communist utopian' municipality transformed since 1979 into a cooperative-based town with near-full employment, equal wages and self-built public housing.

name: Degania Alef
desc: The first kibbutz ever established — the 'mother of the kibbutzim' — whose communal-farming model was followed by 270+ kibbutzim, the most successful large-scale communal movement in history.

name: Kibbutz Lotan
desc: A Reform-Jewish desert kibbutz and one of Israel's flagship ecovillages, renowned for permaculture, straw-bale 'EcoCampus' architecture, solar energy and environmental education.

name: Kibbutz Ketura
desc: A desert kibbutz and leading centre of environmental innovation — home of the Arava Institute and the site of Israel's first commercial solar field.

name: Kibbutz Hatzerim
desc: Founded in the Negev in a single night, this kibbutz is the birthplace of modern drip irrigation — in 1965 it co-founded Netafim, now a global leader active in 110+ countries.

name: Neot Smadar
desc: A desert kibbutz and artists' community blending organic agriculture, craft arts and contemplative self-inquiry, pausing for silence and group reflection through the workday.

name: Kibbutz Sde Eliyahu
desc: A religious kibbutz that is a world pioneer of commercial organic farming and biological pest control; its company BioBee exports beneficial insects worldwide.

name: Kibbutz Ein Gev
desc: A kibbutz on the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee, founded overnight as a 'tower and stockade' settlement and once reachable only by boat; now known for its lakeside resort and music festival.

name: Kibbutz Ginosar
desc: A kibbutz on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, internationally known for the ~2,000-year-old 'Jesus Boat' discovered by its members and displayed at its museum.

name: Nahalal
desc: The first moshav ovdim (workers' cooperative village), famous for its iconic concentric circular plan with public buildings at the hub and farm plots radiating outward.

name: Yodfat
desc: A moshav shitufi (collectively-working cooperative village) in the Lower Galilee that blends communal production with private family households, known for its monkey forest reserve.

name: Kibbutz Samar
desc: A small Arava-desert kibbutz famous as a radical social-anarchist commune: no work roster and no personal budgets — members decide their own work and draw freely from shared resources.

name: Kibbutz Gezer
desc: A pluralistic Reform-Judaism kibbutz with an open synagogue, re-established by young American Jews and listed by the Global Ecovillage Network as it shifts toward sustainability.

name: Kvutzat Kinneret
desc: One of the very first communes of the Zionist labour movement, founded on the Kinneret training farm in 1913 — a seedbed of the whole kibbutz idea, whose pioneers went on to found Degania, Ein Harod and Nahalal.

name: Kibbutz Degania Bet
desc: Founded in 1920 beside Degania Alef, it was the first purpose-planned kibbutz, laid out by architect Fritz Kornberg; an early home of future PM Levi Eshkol.

name: Kibbutz Kfar Giladi
desc: Founded in 1916 by the Hashomer guards' organisation on the northern frontier, one of the oldest kibbutzim, tied to the 1920 Battle of Tel Hai (which it later absorbed).

name: Kibbutz Ein Harod
desc: Founded in 1921 at the foot of Mount Gilboa, Ein Harod was the first LARGE kibbutz and headquarters of HaKibbutz HaMeuhad, the dominant federation; it split in 1952 into Ihud and Meuhad.

name: Kibbutz Tel Yosef
desc: Founded in 1921 by the Gdud HaAvoda labour battalion alongside Ein Harod, and named for fallen hero Joseph Trumpeldor — a centre of the early labour-battalion movement.

name: Kibbutz Geva
desc: A founding-era Jezreel Valley kibbutz established in 1921 near Mount Gilboa — a long-running symbol of the small, intimate kvutza.

name: Kibbutz Gan Shmuel
desc: Recognised as a kibbutz in 1921 on a historic etrog orchard near Hadera, Gan Shmuel became a flagship Hashomer Hatzair kibbutz and a famous citrus producer.

name: Kibbutz Yagur
desc: Founded in 1922 southeast of Haifa, Yagur grew into one of the largest kibbutzim and a HaKibbutz HaMeuhad stronghold; a major Haganah arms cache here was raided on 'Black Sabbath' 1946.

name: Kibbutz Beit Alfa
desc: Founded in 1922 by Hashomer Hatzair pioneers, famous for the nearby 6th-century Beit Alpha synagogue and its spectacular zodiac mosaic, discovered by kibbutz members in 1928.

name: Kibbutz Mizra
desc: A veteran Hashomer Hatzair kibbutz founded in 1923, famous nationwide for its Maadaney Mizra meat plant — for decades Israel's best-known producer of non-kosher (pork) products.

name: Kibbutz Mishmar HaEmek
desc: Founded in 1926, Mishmar HaEmek became the ideological heart of Hashomer Hatzair; in April 1948 its ten-day defence halted the Arab Liberation Army's drive toward Haifa.

name: Kibbutz Givat Brenner
desc: Founded in 1928 and named for writer Yosef Haim Brenner, it grew into the LARGEST kibbutz ever in Israel; co-founded by Enzo Sereni, the Italian-Jewish humanist and parachutist killed at Dachau.

name: Kibbutz Na'an
desc: Founded in 1930, Na'an was the first kibbutz established by native-born Israelis (Sabras); today one of the largest, it built the global NaanDanJain irrigation company.

name: Kibbutz Afikim
desc: Founded in 1932 by pioneers from Soviet Russia, Afikim became one of the largest and wealthiest kibbutzim, built on its renowned Kelet plywood factory.

name: Kibbutz Tirat Zvi
desc: Founded in 1937 as a Tower-and-Stockade settlement, Tirat Zvi is the OLDEST religious kibbutz and the founding community of the Religious Kibbutz Movement; a major date grower in one of Israel's hottest places.

name: Kibbutz Dan
desc: Founded in 1939 at the northern tip of the Hula Valley beneath Mount Hermon, beside biblical Tel Dan and the Dan springs — a frontier kibbutz on the Lebanese/Syrian border.

name: Kibbutz Negba
desc: Founded in 1939 as a Tower-and-Stockade outpost, once the southernmost Jewish settlement; its heroic 1948 stand against repeated Egyptian assaults made it a national symbol.

name: Kibbutz Sdot Yam
desc: A maritime kibbutz founded in 1940 beside ancient Caesarea, pioneering Jewish sea-fishing; its most famous member was poet-paratrooper Hannah Szenes, executed in 1944.

name: Kibbutz Yad Mordechai
desc: Founded in 1943 and named for Warsaw Ghetto Uprising leader Mordechai Anielewicz; its five-day stand against the invading Egyptian army in May 1948 bought crucial time. Famous today for its honey.

name: Kibbutz Revivim
desc: Established in 1943 as one of the 'three lookouts,' Revivim was a pioneering desert-agriculture research station and one of the first Jewish toeholds in the Negev.

name: Kibbutz Be'eri
desc: Founded in 1946 as one of the '11 points in the Negev,' Be'eri became one of the region's largest kibbutzim and home to Israel's leading printing house; it suffered the deadliest single-community massacre of the October 7, 2023 attack.

name: Kibbutz Nirim
desc: Founded in 1946 as one of the '11 points in the Negev,' Nirim held out against the Egyptian army in 1948; on October 7, 2023 it was the first kibbutz terrorists entered and the last relieved.

name: Kibbutz Sasa
desc: Founded in 1949 by North American Hashomer Hatzair pioneers on the Lebanese border, Sasa is famous for Plasan, its kibbutz-owned company that supplies vehicle armour to the U.S. and other militaries.

name: Kibbutz Yotvata
desc: The first kibbutz in the southern Arava desert (1957), famous across Israel for Yotvata Dairy, whose chocolate milk and dairy products are a national icon.

name: Kfar Vitkin
desc: The first Jewish settlement in the Hefer Valley and long the largest moshav in Israel, built around ~150 family farmsteads.

name: Kfar Yehoshua
desc: A western Jezreel Valley moshav (1927) laid out, like neighbouring Nahalal, in architect Richard Kauffmann's distinctive concentric-circle plan.

name: Balfouria
desc: An early Jezreel Valley moshav founded in 1922 by the American Zion Commonwealth and named after Lord Balfour — one of the first settlements financed by American Zionists.

name: Nahalat Yehuda
desc: One of the earliest workers' settlements (1913), an early experiment in cooperative smallholder farming that predates the formal moshav-ovdim model; now a neighbourhood of Rishon LeZion.

name: Merhavia (moshav)
desc: The first modern Jewish settlement in the Jezreel Valley, begun in 1911 as a cooperative on Franz Oppenheimer's principles and converted to a moshav ovdim in 1922.

name: Kfar Hittim
desc: Israel's FIRST moshav shitufi, founded in December 1936 west of Tiberias — pioneering the collective-production / private-family model — and itself a Tower-and-Stockade settlement.

name: Moledet
desc: A Gilboa-region community founded in 1937 as a Tower-and-Stockade settlement by German-Jewish immigrants, which became a moshav shitufi in 1944.

name: Timorim
desc: A southern coastal-plain moshav shitufi near Kiryat Malakhi, reorganised in 1953 as one of the country's first moshavim shitufiim.

name: Be'er Tuvia
desc: One of the country's most prosperous moshavim, re-founded in 1930 on the site of the 1887 First-Aliyah colony Qastina, which had been destroyed in the 1929 riots.

name: Kfar Hess
desc: A Sharon-plain moshav established in 1931 as part of the 'Settlement of the Thousand' programme and the Tel Mond Bloc; named after Moses Hess, an early theorist of Labour Zionism.

name: Beit Yosef
desc: A Beit She'an Valley moshav founded in 1937 as a Tower-and-Stockade settlement during the 1936–39 Arab revolt.

name: Ein Vered
desc: A Sharon-plain moshav founded in 1930 by South African Jews — originally an intensive citrus, field-crop and flower farming community; today it hosts Israel's Tractor Museum.

name: SEKEM
desc: A celebrated sustainable-development community on reclaimed desert NE of Cairo — the first to bring biodynamic agriculture to Egypt — integrating organic farms, businesses, a Waldorf school and a university.

name: Tlholego Ecovillage
desc: One of South Africa's pioneering centres for permaculture, natural building and ecovillage development — created as a model of post-apartheid sustainable rural development.

name: Mbackombel Ecovillage
desc: A flagship of Senegal's pioneering national ecovillage programme — the world's first — which aims to convert 14,000 villages into ecovillages, backed by UNDP and the Global Environment Facility.

name: EcoYoff
desc: A community-led ecovillage initiative in the historic Lebou fishing village of Yoff in Dakar — a long-standing GEN member blending traditional governance with sustainability projects.

name: The Farm
desc: One of America's most famous and enduring communes, founded by seekers who caravanned from San Francisco; once a fully collective economy that peaked near 1,600 residents.

name: Twin Oaks
desc: A secular, egalitarian income-sharing commune and one of the largest and longest-running in North America — originally inspired by B. F. Skinner's 'Walden Two'.

name: East Wind
desc: A secular, democratic income-sharing commune in the Missouri Ozarks where members hold all assets communally — best known for its profitable nut-butter business.

name: Dancing Rabbit Ecovillage
desc: A demonstration ecovillage built around binding ecological covenants governing energy, building materials and vehicle use, on a nonprofit land trust.

name: Earthaven Ecovillage
desc: An off-grid, permaculture-based ecovillage on 329 forested acres in the Blue Ridge Mountains near Asheville, with its own local currency.

name: EcoVillage at Ithaca
desc: A nationally recognized model cohousing ecovillage of ~100 homes in three neighborhoods — concentrating housing on 15 of 175 acres to preserve ~80% of the land.

name: Arcosanti
desc: An experimental 'arcology' (architecture + ecology) town in the high desert, designed by Paolo Soleri as a prototype for dense, car-free, ecologically sound urbanism.

name: Amana Colonies
desc: Seven villages founded by German Radical Pietists who lived communally and self-sufficiently for ~80 years until the 'Great Change' of 1932 — now a National Historic Landmark.

name: Sirius Community
desc: A spiritually focused ecovillage and educational nonprofit on 90 acres in western Massachusetts, founded by former Findhorn members as an American sister community.

name: Lama Foundation
desc: An interfaith spiritual community, retreat and education centre high in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains — famous as the place where Ram Dass wrote 'Be Here Now'.

name: Los Angeles Eco-Village
desc: A pioneering urban intentional community embedded in a dense Koreatown neighborhood, demonstrating how to retrofit existing city blocks for ecological, cooperative living.

name: Ganas
desc: An urban intentional community of ~70–80 people across eleven buildings on Staten Island, organized around 'Feedback Learning' group communication and reuse retail businesses.

name: Acorn Community
desc: An egalitarian, income-sharing, anarchist-feminist commune on a certified-organic farm, sustained chiefly by its heirloom seed business.

name: Sandhill Farm
desc: A small, long-running collective organic farm and income-sharing community in NE Missouri, best known for producing traditional sorghum syrup.

name: N Street Cohousing
desc: The original and best-known 'retrofit' cohousing community in North America, created when neighbors in existing Davis tract houses simply took down their backyard fences.

name: OUR Ecovillage
desc: A 25-acre sustainable-living demonstration site and education centre on Vancouver Island, often called the most built-out permaculture design farm in Canada.

name: Yarrow Ecovillage
desc: A mixed-use ecovillage and cohousing development on a former dairy farm in the Fraser Valley that prompted Chilliwack to create what the mayor called Canada's first 'ecovillage zone'.

name: Whole Village
desc: A 191-acre cooperative farm-based ecovillage NW of Toronto, centred on the shared 'Greenhaven' residence and conceived to preserve farmland from urban sprawl.

name: Bruderhof
desc: A communal Anabaptist Christian movement of ~3,000 members across ~24 communities on four continents, fully sharing possessions and income and practising pacifism.

name: Crystal Waters
desc: Widely regarded as the world's first intentional permaculture village, north of Brisbane — it pioneered low-impact rural subdivision design and won the 1996 UN World Habitat Award.

name: Narara Ecovillage
desc: An intergenerational residential cooperative on a former government horticultural research station on the NSW Central Coast, with shared renewable-energy infrastructure.

name: Moora Moora
desc: One of Australia's longest-running intentional communities, an off-grid cooperative of clustered hamlets atop Mount Toolebewong, surrounded by protected forest.

name: Aldinga Arts EcoVillage
desc: An arts-focused ecovillage ~45 km south of Adelaide, blending low-energy housing with a strong creative culture, communal orchards and an organic farm.

name: Atamai Village
desc: A permaculture-based ecovillage near Motueka, explicitly designed for resilience to peak oil, climate change and food insecurity — a modern self-reliant village.

name: Tui Community
desc: An intentional community on a former farm bordering Abel Tasman National Park, sharing daily life and a communal garden — and birthplace of the Tui Balms natural-products cooperative.

name: Earthsong Eco-Neighbourhood
desc: New Zealand's first cohousing community, built on permaculture principles — 32 homes sharing extensive common facilities, internationally recognised as a model of sustainable urban living.

name: Wilderland
desc: One of New Zealand's oldest alternative communities — an anarchist, vegetarian back-to-the-land settlement that established one of the country's earliest organic farms.

name: Huehuecóyotl
desc: Mexico's oldest ecovillage, founded by a multinational collective of artists, ecologists and educators who had toured as the 'Illuminated Elephants' theatre troupe.

name: Las Cañadas
desc: An internationally recognised agroecology and permaculture cooperative in one of the last remnants of central Veracruz's cloud forest, transformed from a cattle ranch.

name: Comunidad Los Horcones
desc: Founded in 1973, Los Horcones describes itself as the only true 'Walden Two' community, applying B. F. Skinner's behavioral science to the design of its culture.

name: Aldea Feliz
desc: One of Colombia's best-known ecovillages, ~90 minutes from Bogotá — a reference point and education hub within the Colombian and CASA Latina ecovillage networks.

name: Ecocentro IPEC
desc: A pioneering centre for permaculture and bioconstruction in Brazil's cerrado — a living laboratory that trained a generation of Brazilian permaculturists.

name: Comunidad Inti Wara Yassi
desc: A Bolivian community and NGO that rescues wildlife from illegal trafficking and runs three sanctuaries — a live-in, volunteer-driven community caring for rescued animals.

name: Kovcheg Ecovillage
desc: One of the oldest and largest of Russia's Anastasia-inspired 'kin's domain' settlements, ~140 km SW of Moscow, allocating one-hectare family homesteads and serving as a model for the movement.

name: Grishino Ecovillage
desc: One of Russia's pioneering ecovillages, in a historic northern village ~300 km NE of St. Petersburg, blending traditional Russian wooden architecture with permaculture and eco-education.

name: Lilleoru
desc: An Estonian study-and-living centre and ecovillage founded just after independence, ~25 km from Tallinn, supporting conscious human development; a GEN member.

name: Aurora Community
desc: An international eco-spiritual community and sustainability learning centre in the Carpathian Mountains that helped catalyse Romania's growing ecovillage movement.

name: Hutterite Colonies
desc: A communitarian Anabaptist movement living in large-scale communal 'colonies' across the Canadian prairies and northern US — one of the largest and most enduring communal movements on Earth.
